live_proof: inspection with line numbers in the 3.22.0 tree: sqlite3Fts3Offsets() saves a poslist pointer per phrase and reads it at fts3_snippet.c:1544, while fts3EvalRestart at fts3.c:5540 frees and reloads already-visited doclists. Fixed upstream in 3.49.0

lifetime_ender: an incremental phrase restarts the NEAR group, so fts3EvalRestart frees and reloads the doclists those pointers refer to

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: CheriBSD 15.0-CURRENT riscv64-purecap, memsys5 over the case's static arena (shared/run-cheribsd.py --mode nested). Revocation acts on a guest malloc free, and under memsys5 there is none: sqlite3_free returns the block to memsys5's own pool inside one array the guest allocator sees as a single live object. So a tag fault here is NOT revocation reporting, and since 2026-10-30 it is not scored as a catch either: this arm is judged by the mechanism rule the virtual arms carry in tools/arms.json (catch_causes), under which an access the mechanism did not reject is MISSED however the program then crashes. A SIGPROT(34) si_code=2 at the function host ASan reported (fault_sites) is MISSED with the fault kept in its note; a fault anywhere else is not tied to the defect and stays NO-READING:unattributed. What the rule rests on is the configuration and not a silence: SQLITE_CONFIG_HEAP puts every SQLite allocation inside sqlite_heap[], sqlite3_free returns the block to memsys5's own pool, and no free() ever reaches the guest allocator for a sweep to act on. The same harness with SYSALLOC=1 does emit allocator=system revoke=on-every-free on 31 of 33 cases (results/2026-10-29-cheribsd/non-nested), so the revoking path is live where it exists

Every SQLite object is one of the guest malloc's, so its end IS a free the quarantine sees and revocation can act. SIGPROT(34) at the function host ASan reported (fault_sites), or the case returns and this arm did not see it. The cell is a reading of this arm only if the run records allocator=system and revoke=on-every-free for the case, which is repro_init()'s NOMEM5 branch saying it ran: a case whose run_case() does its own sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_HEAP) never calls repro_init() at all, so NOMEM5 does nothing to it and what ran was the nested configuration under the stock quarantine. 31 of the 33 record the marker; the two that do not are 07 and 22, the same two the Capstone builder reports not applicable, and both are NO-READING:out-of-denominator here for the same reason

note: WITHDRAWN 2026-10-30, by the rule 01 and 09 were already withdrawn under: a trigger that does not reach the defect it names is not a measurement of that defect, whatever the defect's own standing. The rule is now applied uniformly across this corpus -- 02, 11 and 13 carried the same 2026-10-11 finding and were CORRECTED instead, each with a replaced trigger that reaches its defect and a reading to show it; 08 is the one where no correction was found, so it leaves the denominator rather than sitting in it as a miss. The evidence is three readings that agree: host ASan SILENT and returned (results/2026-10-11-host-asan), the gdb ordering below, and the 2026-10-29 run, where every one of the five arms reports MISSED with its controls behaving as its configuration declares -- including virtual-nested-pools, which catches 19 of the other 19 counted temporal cases in that same run, and cheribsd-platform, which catches 13. An arm that finds the other cases and not this one is evidence about the trigger. Upstream 51dd67080a ships no test and calls it a potential use-after-free, so there is no upstream shape to copy. The structural reason a correction was not found, which is an explanation of the gdb finding and not a second measurement: phrases in a NEAR group advance together, so whenever a sibling restarts the earlier phrase's saved pointer is already nil. The defect is not disputed and the case is not deleted -- the directory and its number are kept so that every record written against them stays resolvable, and so that the silicon and vp2 arms, whose bundles are keyed to this numbering, are not broken. A trigger that reaches it would bring the case back. It is out of the corpus's denominator; see README.md. || Trigger does not reach the defect (2026-10-11, gdb on the host -O0 build): sqlite3Fts3Offsets runs twice and all three fts3EvalRestart calls come after both of them, so no saved poslist pointer is ever read across a restart. Upstream 51dd67080a fixes it by cancelling the incremental phrases BEFORE the pointers are taken (sqlite3Fts3MsrCancel from a new fts3ExprRestartIfCb), which is the ordering this trigger never produces.
